stories.summary: Let plan owners and delegates patch, pause, interrupt and close their own plans
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: combined impact run 2026-10-30 on master 5c8f8ac (rough stand-ins of all 19 Phase B stories in one scratch worktree; final run 19053 passed, 0 failed) - 3 conflicts (test_decision_answer_ownership NOT_OWNED_ACTIONS, test_ownership_policy delegate parametrize, test_policy_local::test_owner_still_cannot_pause_its_plan), pre-authorized below.

WHAT: `app/policy.py` `LocalPolicy.allow` grants a plan's owner and delegates (beyond the local operator) only five actions: plan:approve, plan:reject, plan:dispatch, story:merge, decision:answer. Every other action is local-operator only, so a remote (OIDC) owner of a plan cannot patch a story, pause/resume it, interrupt it, mark it done or edit its role_config. The operator decided (2026-10-30) to extend owner authority to the plan-scoped actions as well.

CHANGE (app/policy.py): in the ownership tuple inside `LocalPolicy.allow` (the block that currently lists `Action.PLAN_APPROVE, Action.PLAN_REJECT, Action.PLAN_DISPATCH, Action.STORY_MERGE, Action.DECISION_ANSWER`), add `Action.STORY_PATCH`, `Action.STORY_INTERRUPT`, `Action.STORY_MARK_DONE`, `Action.PLAN_PAUSE` and `Action.CONFIG_WRITE`. Update the comment above it ("exactly the five actions a plan's owner governs") to say ten, and the class docstring's list of owner actions to match. Do not touch the system-principal branch or the PLAN_INGEST branch.

WHY CONFIG_WRITE IS SAFE: host-scoped writes (`set_role_default`, `record_security_audit`) are decided through `pipeline/authorization.py` `refusal_for_host_config`, which passes `resource_for({}, "", None)` - a resource with an empty owner and no delegates - so the `resource.owner and ...` guard never matches and host-wide config stays local-operator only. Only plan-scoped `config:write` (`patch_plan`, `set_plan_role_config`, on a plan that has an owner) is newly granted to its owner.

DOCS (docs/adr/0009-tenancy-and-authorization-model.md): append a section `## Amendment 2026-10-30: owner authority covers plan-scoped actions` stating the ten owner/delegate actions, that host-scoped config:write stays local-operator only (empty-owner resource), and why (a standalone server has no local operator at the client, so remote owners need to run their own plans end to end).

DOCS (docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md) MUST change in this same story: it is the canonical spec that pins the boundary this story moves. Rewrite the `LocalPolicy` table row that says the ownership grant is 'exactly the five actions its owner governs' / 'scoped to those five actions only' to the ten owner/delegate actions, and rewrite the prose block that lists `plan:approve`, `plan:reject`, `plan:dispatch`, `story:merge` and `decision:answer` as the whole grant, including removing the '`plan:pause` stays outside the ownership grant on purpose' rationale. Mirror the ADR 0009 amendment wording. This file IS in the story's `files` scope - the scope gate will not flag it, and leaving it stale is a Blocking review finding.

3. tests/unit/test_policy_local.py: replace the whole function `test_owner_still_cannot_pause_its_plan` (comment "The deliberate boundary: `plan:pause` stays outside the ownership grant." and `assert ... Action.PLAN_PAUSE, resource) is False`) with `test_owner_may_pause_its_plan`, comment "ADR 0009 amendment 2026-10-30: plan:pause is inside the ownership grant.", same resource, asserting `is True`.
The impact run confirmed these are the only existing tests the change breaks.

stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: combined impact run 2026-10-30 on master 5c8f8ac (rough stand-ins of all 19 Phase B stories in one scratch worktree; final run 19053 passed, 0 failed) - 0 conflicts. A first draft that also gated decompose_plan and advance_all_plans here broke 5 structural/enforcement tests; that scope moved to the remote tool policy story.

WHAT: `PipelineService.get_effective_config` (pipeline/service.py) returns host environment values (`env`, `ignored_env_vars`) and filesystem paths (`sources`: launchd plist, MCP config, registry path). A remote caller must not see those; it needs only the role routing. Local stdio (LOCAL_OPERATOR) and every other caller keep the full result.

NEW MODULE pipeline/remote_scope.py (pipeline/service.py is at 956 lines; later stories also add a few lines there, so keep logic in this module):
- `is_network_principal(principal) -> bool`: True exactly when `principal.auth_method == "oidc"` (app/oidc.py builds remote principals with auth_method "oidc"; LOCAL_OPERATOR is "shared-secret", system principals "system", ANONYMOUS "none"). Keep it one explicit check; do not invert it to "not local", because the scheduler binds SYSTEM_SCHEDULER.
- `remote_effective_config(result: dict, plan_name) -> dict`: when `plan_name` is None or empty, return `{"ok": False, "error": "plan_name is required for a remote caller"}`; otherwise return only `{"ok": result.get("ok"), "roles": result.get("roles")}`.

Otherwise unchanged. Plan visibility for remote callers is enforced before the handler by the remote tool policy (a later story), not here.

SCOPE IS DECIDED, NOT A FINDING: `app/dashboard_routes.py` is in this story's `files` scope because the dashboard's `GET /api/config` route calls the same `_get_effective_config_impl` and is reachable by a remote (OIDC) dashboard session - so it leaks `env` and `sources` by the same path this story closes for MCP callers. Apply the same remote scoping there and test it. - with a plan name -> keys are exactly {"ok", "roles"} and no "env"/"sources";

stories.summary: Load model, forge and repo credentials from mounted secret files in the entrypoint
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: combined impact run 2026-10-30 on master 5c8f8ac (rough stand-ins of all 19 Phase B stories in one scratch worktree; final run 19053 passed, 0 failed) - 0 conflicts attributable to this story.

WHAT: deploy/entrypoint.sh takes no credentials today except the OIDC client secret file. Read the operator's credentials from mounted files, export them only as needed, and set the repo defaults SA-05 relies on.

CHANGE (deploy/entrypoint.sh; POSIX sh, `set -eu` stays):
- A function `load_secret <ENV_NAME> <FILE_ENV_NAME> <default path>`: the path is `${<FILE_ENV_NAME>:-<default>}`. If the file does not exist OR is empty (zero bytes, or only whitespace) do nothing - compose `secrets:` requires every listed file to exist, so the installer creates unused ones empty (a missing or empty credential is not an error; the backend that needs it fails closed when used). If it exists: refuse (die) when it is not a regular file, when `stat -c %a` shows any group/other bit (mode & 077 != 0), or when its owner uid (`stat -c %u`) is not the current uid (`id -u`); otherwise read it with `IFS= read -r` / `cat`, strip a trailing newline, and export ENV_NAME. Never echo the value; log only "loaded <ENV_NAME> from secret file".
- Calls, defaults under /run/secrets:
  - `PIPELINE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_FILE` (/run/secrets/anthropic_api_key). NOTE the exported name is PIPELINE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, not ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: app/backend_claude.py strips an ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY on purpose, and story "Pass an operator-supplied Anthropic API key to the claude CLI without allowing provider redirects" reads this explicit variable instead.
  - `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN_FILE` (/run/secrets/claude_code_oauth_token).
  - `GH_TOKEN` from `GH_TOKEN_FILE` (/run/secrets/gh_token); when GH_TOKEN ends up set and PIPELINE_FORGE is unset, export PIPELINE_FORGE=github.
  - `OLLAMA_API_KEY` from `OLLAMA_API_KEY_FILE` (/run/secrets/ollama_api_key).
  - When `PIPELINE_GIT_TOKEN_FILE` is unset and /run/secrets/gh_token exists, export `PIPELINE_GIT_TOKEN_FILE=/run/secrets/gh_token` (repo_clone reads the path, not the value).
- Repo defaults: `PIPELINE_REPOS_ROOT="${PIPELINE_REPOS_ROOT:-/var/lib/pipeline/repos}"`, create it (`mkdir -p`, mode 0750) and export it; `PIPELINE_ALLOWED_REPO_ROOTS="${PIPELINE_ALLOWED_REPO_ROOTS:-$PIPELINE_REPOS_ROOT}"`, exported.
- Place all of this after the existing variable defaults/exports and before the OIDC secret check and the process starts.

DOCS (deploy/README.md): add a "Credentials" subsection listing the four secret files, their default paths, the 0600/owner requirement, which variable each becomes, and the repo defaults.

TESTS: new file tests/smoke/test_entrypoint_secrets.py that runs deploy/entrypoint.sh's `load_secret` in a subprocess. To make it testable, guard the process-starting tail of the script with `if [ "${PIPELINE_ENTRYPOINT_SOURCE_ONLY:-0}" = 1 ]; then return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0; fi` placed right before the first process start, and source the script under `sh -c '. deploy/entrypoint.sh; ...'` with PIPELINE_ENTRYPOINT_SOURCE_ONLY=1 and PIPELINE_IDENTITY_PROVIDER=none-for-test (or whatever value skips the OIDC check - read the script). Cases: a 0600 file owned by the test uid is exported (assert via `printenv`), and the value never appears on stderr; a 0644 file makes the script exit non-zero with a message naming the variable but not the value; a missing file and an empty file each leave the variable unset and exit 0; GH_TOKEN set and PIPELINE_FORGE unset -> PIPELINE_FORGE=github; PIPELINE_FORGE=gitlab preset is kept; PIPELINE_ALLOWED_REPO_ROOTS defaults to PIPELINE_REPOS_ROOT and a preset value is kept.

stories.summary: Pass an operator-supplied Anthropic API key to the claude CLI without allowing provider redirects
Send OLLAMA_API_KEY as a bearer token on every Ollama request
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: combined impact run 2026-10-30 on master 5c8f8ac (rough stand-ins of all 19 Phase B stories in one scratch worktree; final run 19053 passed, 0 failed) - 0 conflicts when the headers keyword is spread only while OLLAMA_API_KEY is set; about 60 failures when it is passed unconditionally (see below).

WHAT: to use https://ollama.com directly (no local Ollama daemon in the container), requests need `Authorization: Bearer <OLLAMA_API_KEY>`. No Ollama call sends a header today. A local `http://host.docker.internal:11434` endpoint needs no key, and nothing may change when the variable is unset.

CHANGE:
- app/inference_providers.py: add a module-level helper `ollama_auth_kwargs() -> dict` returning `{"headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}}` when `os.environ.get("OLLAMA_API_KEY", "").strip()` is non-empty, else `{}`, and spread it (`**ollama_auth_kwargs()`) into the three Ollama-provider httpx calls in the Ollama provider class: `httpx.post(f"{endpoint}/api/chat", ...)`, `httpx.get(f"{endpoint}/api/ps", ...)` and `httpx.get(f"{endpoint}/api/tags", ...)`. Do not add it to the LM Studio / MLX / OpenAI-compatible providers.
- scripts/local_agent_chat.py and scripts/local_agent_oracle_chat.py: each has one `httpx.stream("POST", f"{origin['ENDPOINT']}/api/chat", json=payload, ...)` call. Spread `**origin["inference_providers"].ollama_auth_kwargs()` into it (the `origin` dict already carries the inference_providers module - read how `get_local_provider` is reached on the same lines). If `origin` does not carry it, import `ollama_auth_kwargs` from `app.inference_providers` the way the file imports other app modules.
- Never log the header or the key.

TESTS (new file tests/unit/test_ollama_api_key_header.py):
- ollama_auth_kwargs() is {} when unset and when blank/whitespace, and {"headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer k"}} when set to " k " (value stripped);
- the Ollama provider's chat sends the header when set (monkeypatch `app.inference_providers.httpx.post` with a fake capturing kwargs) and passes NO `headers` keyword at all when unset;
- loaded_models and reachable send the header when set;
- the streaming path in scripts/local_agent_chat.py sends it (monkeypatch httpx.stream with a context-manager fake; follow tests/unit/test_local_agent_streaming_and_provider.py for how that module is driven).
WHY THE KWARG IS SPREAD, NOT ALWAYS PASSED: about 60 existing tests (tests/unit/test_inference_providers.py, test_backend_role_routing_complete.py, test_backend_tuning_knobs.py, test_backend_resource_status.py, test_acceptance_ollama_chat_retry.py, ...) fake httpx.post/get/stream with fixed signatures that reject an unexpected `headers` keyword. The impact run showed they all pass when the keyword is added only while OLLAMA_API_KEY is set. Do not modify those tests, and do not pass `headers=` unconditionally.

stories.summary: Publish RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata from the remote MCP transport
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: combined impact run 2026-10-30 on master 5c8f8ac (rough stand-ins of all 19 Phase B stories in one scratch worktree; final run 19053 passed, 0 failed) - 0 conflicts attributable to this story.

WHAT: MCP clients (Claude Code checks RFC 9728 `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` first, then RFC 8414) discover the authorization server from the resource server. `pipeline/remote_transport.py` only verifies bearer tokens; its 401 sends `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` with no metadata pointer, so a client cannot start its login flow.

CHANGE (pipeline/remote_transport.py, 446 lines):
- New env var `PIPELINE_MCP_RESOURCE_URL` (e.g. `https://pipeline.example.com/mcp`). Validate it in `serve()` before opening a socket: must be an absolute `https://` URL with no query/fragment/userinfo; if unset, metadata is disabled and behaviour is exactly as today. Invalid -> SystemExit naming the variable.
- In `BearerAuthMiddleware.__call__`, before credential checks (after the lifespan/non-http branches): an HTTP `GET` whose path is `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` or `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` + the resource URL's path (RFC 9728 section 3.1 path-suffixed form) is answered unauthenticated, when metadata is enabled, with 200 `application/json`:
  `{"resource": <PIPELINE_MCP_RESOURCE_URL>, "authorization_servers": [<PIPELINE_OIDC_ISSUER>], "bearer_methods_supported": ["header"], "scopes_supported": ["openid"]}`. Any other method on that path -> 405. It must not count against the failed-auth rate limiter and must not write an auth audit record. When metadata is disabled the path falls through to the normal 401.
- The 401 challenge (`_send_unauthorized`) becomes `Bearer resource_metadata="<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource<resource path>"` when metadata is enabled, plain `Bearer` otherwise. Pass the value into the middleware via its constructor (environ is already passed) rather than a global.
- Keep the file under 1000 lines.

Deferred to "Write the standalone deployment guide" - not a finding: operator documentation of PIPELINE_MCP_RESOURCE_URL lives in docs/DEPLOY_STANDALONE.md. Put this line verbatim in the PR description.

TESTS (new file tests/unit/test_remote_transport_resource_metadata.py), driving the ASGI middleware directly with a stub inner app and a stub provider (follow tests/unit/test_remote_transport*.py):
- metadata enabled: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource without Authorization -> 200 and the exact JSON keys/values; GET with the /mcp suffix -> same; POST -> 405; the inner app is never called;
- metadata enabled: an unauthenticated POST /mcp -> 401 with header www-authenticate containing `resource_metadata="https://pipeline.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`;
- metadata disabled (unset): GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource -> 401 with plain `Bearer`;
- serve()-time validation: http://..., a URL with `?x`, a URL with `user@` and a relative path each raise SystemExit naming PIPELINE_MCP_RESOURCE_URL (test the validation helper directly; do not open sockets);
- many metadata GETs from one IP do not trip the failed-auth limiter (a subsequent bad-token request still gets 401, not 429).
